previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, recent CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for leg swelling and weight gain due to decompensated diastolic heart failure. She had a history of urinary retention requiring a catheter and was on bethanechol, which contributed to diarrhea. Hyperkalemia and hyponatremia on admission resolved with diuresis. A scheduled left lower extremity angiogram was postponed due to kidney concerns. She improved with IV lasix, weight decreased, and electrolytes normalized. Coccygeal pain from a recent fall was managed with acetaminophen. She was discharged home with instructions to hold torsemide and warfarin before the rescheduled vascular procedure and to monitor daily weights.

For full details, please see the dictated operative report. In brief, the right CFA was accessed with cannulation of the left external iliac artery and subsequent left lower extremity arteriogram. Intra-op Findings: 1. Patent common femoral, profunda femoris, SFA with a couple of areas of non-hemodynamically significant stenosis. There is 2 vessel runoff to the lower leg. The posterior tibial artery is occluded. 2. The anterior tibial artery is patent all the way to the foot and provides blood supply mainly to the forefoot. The hindfoot has very poor blood supply. Based on the findings as above, it was decided to perform no concurrent intervention. She tolerated the procedure well and went to the PACU and then to the floor in good condition. Her diet was rapidly advanced. Pain was well-controlled on oral pain meds. Home medicines were resumed immediately post-operatively save for warfarin; she will resume this medicine following her discharge on POD#1.
